## India: Regulatory Updates & DPDPA Implementation

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Minister confirmed that the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules have been finalized and are slated for publication in the coming days, marking a crucial step towards full implementation of the Act. MeitY Secretary further reiterated that there will be no extensions for DPDPA compliance deadlines, urging all entities, including startups, to ensure their readiness. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

The Centre also issued the Digital Personal Data Protection (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026, providing clarity on critical aspects such as consent mechanisms and data audit provisions under the DPDPA. This order aims to streamline the compliance process for data fiduciaries. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikAFBVV95cUxQcERvUDdVMmIyWFpuT0VBYjlRYlhmenJyYVQ3MkRvTjg4a0ZHVFgxRjkyZlFaOHp5T3BDdFBBRWFSMWlBbmw1ODZnZFFUc1BCbHJYQm9CTDdiNVdEU2JXbFFkdW5IZ1hSV0hwTFJscV9kMF9WcEgwYWpSSXBxU0JfRVlYWkJOTW1MU3hZandaUUc?oc=5)) Questions are being raised about the preparedness of government ministries and state bodies to meet the extensive data protection compliance requirements mandated by the DPDPA. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5)) Separately, MeitY informed Parliament that Common Service Centre (CSC) operators are strictly prohibited from storing sensitive Aadhaar or banking data, reinforcing data handling restrictions for such services. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

## India: Sectoral Compliance & Emerging Issues

The financial sector is actively responding to the DPDPA, with a major Indian bank reportedly investing over ₹50 crore in its compliance initiatives. Discussions also highlight the combined data protection demands from DPDPA, RBI, and SEBI on the digital Indian workforce. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxNWFV4aWc1d2ktNWp4elg4TXJpbnRtVVdIWkxRakg0bWN6NURDclVrM
